lecture_summary: The lecture develops rolling-without-slipping kinematics and energy methods, then introduces angular momentum, its relationship to external torque, and its conservation. It applies these ideas to a hollow sphere rolling down a ramp and to rotationally inelastic interactions involving rain entering rotating cups and a bullet embedding in a cylinder.

videos.title: Rotational Motion Physics, Basic Introduction, Angular Velocity & Tangential Acceleration
videos.reason: Builds the rolling-kinematics foundation: period, angular velocity and acceleration, and rotational–translational relationships underlying v = ωR and a = αR.

videos.title: Rotational Kinetic Energy and Moment of Inertia Examples & Physics Problems
videos.reason: The strongest match for the hollow-sphere ramp method: apply energy conservation to rolling objects on inclines while including rotational kinetic energy and moment of inertia.

videos.title: Angular Momentum - Basic Introduction, Torque, Inertia, Conservation of Angular Momentum
videos.reason: Provides the conceptual framework linking linear and angular momentum, external torque, rotational inertia, and angular-momentum conservation.

videos.title: Angular Momentum Physics Practice Problems
videos.reason: Adds representative calculations with disks, rods, and a child joining a merry-go-round—the closest playlist analogue to added or sticking mass changing a rotating system’s inertia and angular speed.

coverage_gaps: No strong match explicitly covers the cycloid traced by a rim point or derives the no-slip condition from circumference and period.
The rolling-energy video’s metadata does not explicitly cover the thin-shell result I = 2mR²/3 or explain why ideal static friction enforces rolling without dissipating mechanical energy.
No listed description explicitly covers particle angular momentum as r × p, including its sin φ dependence, or a tangential bullet embedding in a cylinder.
No exact match covers rain entering rotating cups or explicitly calculates thermal/internal-energy gain in a rotational sticking collision; the merry-go-round problem is the closest analogue.
